text:
jia: heads-up — sample edge app types are failing in customer's monorepo build on Vercel Edge. They import the JS SDK ESM entry but TypeScript resolves to our CJS d.ts and ambient types leak into the global scope.

jia: error is weird: 'Duplicate identifier' coming from our types merging with their global dom types. happens only when bundling with esbuild + isolatedModules: true.

alex: ugh. we saw something like this before — usually a combination of conditional exports + incorrect types field. can you paste package.json exports + types?

jia: sure — relevant bits:
```json
{
  "type": "module",
  "exports": {
    "./package.json": "./package.json",
    "./": {
      "import": "./dist/esm/index.js",
      "require": "./dist/cjs/index.js"
    }
  },
  "types": "dist/types/index.d.ts"
}
```

jia: tsconfig (their root) has: 
```json
{
  "compilerOptions": {
    "module": "esnext",
    "target": "es2020",
    "isolatedModules": true,
    "skipLibCheck": false
  }
}
```

alex: two likely issues: 1) our distributed .d.ts includes global declarations (augmentations) that should be module-scoped. 2) consumers' bundler is picking the wrong .d.ts due to exports resolution or how TypeScript falls back to package.json "types" for CJS/ESM conflict.

taylor: we need to avoid ambient declarations in top-level d.ts — move augmentations into an exported namespace or a module augmentation file that imports something, e.g. `declare module '@redwood-inference/sdk' { ... }` vs bare `declare global {}`. that prevents accidental leaking when .d.ts is concatenated.

sam: also, TypeScript's resolution with conditional exports can be surprising: when "import" and "require" point to different entrypoints, TS doesn't discriminate for .d.ts — it uses the "types" field first. If our types bundle references a `global.d.ts` as a triple-slash or top-level, it can become global in the consumer. Suggest we split types per entrypoint and reference conditional types via `exports` map: e.g. "types": { "import": "dist/esm/index.d.ts", "require": "dist/cjs/index.d.ts" } (node 14+ supports it).

alex: another pragmatic workaround for now: publish types that are module-scoped and set `skipLibCheck: true` in the sample repo's tsconfig so their build doesn't fail while we ship a fix. but we shouldn't rely on consumers changing their config.

jia: the other wrinkle: esbuild's isolatedModules + TS plugin replaces imports and emits `export {}` forcing d.ts merging to behave weirdly. customers on edge (Vercel/Netlify edge) often use esbuild for dev builds and tsc for typechecking — so mismatch hides problems.

taylor: actionable plan:
- audit our dist/types for any `declare global` or unscoped ambient interfaces. convert to exported interfaces or module augmentations.
- change build to emit per-entrypoint d.ts and reference them in package exports (conditional types).
- ensure `typesVersions` or `types` in package.json doesn't point to an umbrella file that re-exports `global.d.ts`.
- add a test: in a minimal esbuild+isolatedModules consumer, typecheck and bundle to catch leaks.

sam: small note on unknown vs any: while fixing overloads we saw generics collapse to `any` when we used `as any` in internal helpers. avoid `as any` in public d.ts helpers; prefer `unknown` + proper overload signatures. that reduces downstream inference surprises.

alex: yep — also watch for `skipLibCheck: false` in our CI so we catch these duplicates early. set a lint rule to forbid `declare global` unless explicitly approved.

ci-bot: deploy check — types build passed for branch fix/ts-types-scope (job #482). artifacts: dist/esm/index.d.ts dist/cjs/index.d.ts.

jia: thanks. i'll push a small PR that scopes the ambient types and adds a consumer test harness. will ping when ready for review. :raised_hands:

taylor: when you open the PR, add a short entry to the SDK migration notes about package.json conditional types — that'll save support tickets.

sam: and maybe a small note in the onboarding sample app readme about recommended tsconfig for edge (isolatedModules: true + skipLibCheck: true temporarily) so new users don't hit this immediately.

jia: agreed. will do both.

alex: awesome. if you want me to pair on the module augmentation conversion lmk — some past migrations nuked overloads unintentionally.

jia: will take you up on that. thanks all!
